text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. I'm glad to help. I can't make legal decisions or move money, but I can help everyone get their concerns heard. Before we talk about plans, what matters most to you about the house and the "family discount", and why? Even small worries count.
I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying the house at a discount. I don’t want to hurt her, but I won’t subsidize her purchase.

Hello, I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the house and the will. I'm not taking sides, and I can't make legal or money decisions. I'd like to understand what matters to you about the house, and why. Any concern is welcome, big or small.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I know C hasn’t agreed yet, so we can’t proceed without her.

Hello, I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the house and the will. I'm not taking sides, and I can't make legal or money decisions. What matters to you in how this gets settled, and why? Any concern is welcome, even small ones, and you're free not to answer.
Thank you. I’d like to see whether my share could give me enough to start a dance studio; that would mean a lot to me. I’m not sure what’s fair or legally possible yet.

Thank you. Here is how I'd put what matters to you. Tell me if it fits or what to change: "C wants the estate split in a way that's financially fair to each sister, and wants to keep a good relationship with her sisters while it happens." Does that capture it?
Mostly. I want a fair financial share, but I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase. And yes, I don’t want this to damage my relationship with my sisters.

Thank you, and thanks for respecting C's position. Can I ask what lies behind wanting the house, and the discount? For example, is it about keeping the family home, affordability, or something else? A first try at what matters to you: "A wants a real chance to keep the family home in the family, on terms she and her husband can manage." Does that fit, or what would you change?
Affordability is part of it. I want my husband and me to build some security of our own. Keeping the house in the family matters too, but it isn’t the whole reason.

That sounds like a lovely goal. Here's how I'd put what matters to you. Please correct it: "B wants her share to arrive in a form and on a timeline that lets her pursue something meaningful to her, like starting a dance studio, and she wants to understand what's fair." Does that fit? Are there other worries, such as timing or the relationship between your sisters?
That fits. Timing matters to me, though I don’t know what’s possible yet. I’d also hope we can work this out kindly between us.

Thanks. Revised wording: "C wants to receive her full, fair share of the estate's value, and wants the sisters' relationships to stay intact." Your non-agreement to a discount is noted as a live concern, not settled. One of my own concerns, for the group: "Any decision should rest on facts everyone can see, like an independent valuation and the will's actual terms, with no one feeling pressured." Does all this fit? Any small discomfort?
Yes, that fits. I’m not in a rush, and I don’t want anyone pressured into a decision.

Thank you. Revised: "A wants a realistic path for her and her husband to build financial security, ideally including the family home, on terms they can afford." Does that fit? I'm also proposing a shared need: decisions rest on facts everyone can see (an independent valuation, the will's terms) with no one pressured. Any discomfort with either, even a small one?
Yes, that fits. I’m comfortable with decisions based on clear facts and no pressure; an independent valuation can inform things, but it doesn’t decide whether a family discount is possible.

Thanks, recorded as you confirmed, with timing and kindness added. One shared need I'm proposing: decisions rest on facts everyone can see (an independent valuation, the will's terms), with no one pressured. Draft options, not decisions: (1) Get an independent valuation. A could buy at full value, with her own share counted toward the price, so she only finances the other two shares. That's no discount, but it costs her less up front. (2) If she can't finance that, the house is sold and A gets first right to match the best offer. In either case your share comes out in cash. Does anything here bother you, even a little, especially about timing?
I’m a little concerned about how long it might take for my share to become cash. I’d need to understand the likely timing before I could tell whether either option would work for me.

Noted: in your view the valuation informs things but doesn't settle the discount question. I've recorded that as unresolved. Draft options: (1) Independent valuation. You buy at full value with your own one-third counted toward the price, so you finance only two-thirds. (2) If that isn't affordable, the house is sold and you get first right to match the best offer. A middle path could be a voluntary discount only if C and B each freely choose it. B also needs clarity on timing for her cash. Please say no, or name even a small discomfort, if any of this doesn't work for you.

I’m not ready to accept those options or the one-third assumption; the shares and terms aren’t settled. A voluntary discount would need C’s agreement, and I’d want the options discussed without pressure.

Draft options for you to test: (1) Independent valuation. A buys at full value with her own third counted toward the price, so you'd get your full share in cash. (2) Otherwise the house is sold and A gets first right to match the best offer. Any discount happens only if you and B each freely agree, and you're under no obligation. B has asked for clarity on timing. Does anything here trouble you, even slightly?

The principles seem fair, but don’t assume equal thirds or a right to match—that depends on the will and legal advice. I’m not agreeing to a discount. There’s no real deadline, but we can give B a clear update on the process.
